setlist.title: Beat It On Down The Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (2 reviews): Phil and Billy's jam leading into the song is daring, with Phil playing around with Billy at the intro; Reviewer points to a roughly 22-minute version of the song, which they call 'Around' [3][6]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): Reviewer calls the stand-alone first-set Stella intense, with Jerry letting it shine [11]
- **Playin' In The Band** (1 review): Donna sings along on this song [6]

## Setlist highlights

- Earliest performances in the archive: WRS Prelude [12]

## The recordings

- **gd1972-07-21.148725.sbd.bear.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): soundboard; 24 songs; 181 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]. Said about its sound: Described as a significant upgrade; compare the sound on Cumberland Blues [11]
- **gd72-07-21.sbd.cotsman.9246.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 25 songs; 181 min; rated 3.25/5 by 8 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the recording quality is weak and holds back an otherwise excellent show; suspects a better-sounding copy exists; Sound is not top notch but very listenable; the playing is of the highest quality; Recording quality falls short of the performance [3][4][5][8][9]

## Around the show

- Band took the stage just after 8:00; with a break, the show ended in time for fans to catch last buses downtown [5]
- Bob Weir introduces the newest member of the musical family for vocals: Donna, who sings along [6]
- First set ran nearly two and a half hours including tunings; a Promised Land opener went unrecorded [10]
- Three Weir tunes come in a row early; the mellow first set features his ballads [11]
- Same material as shnid 9246 but with solid provenance [1]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1972-07-21.148725.sbd.bear.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Bear, Tim Dalton; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Bear's Master Soundboard Cassettes > 1st generation Cassettes > 2nd generation Cassettes > Tim Dalton's Dat (16/48) [1]
- **gd72-07-21.sbd.cotsman.9246.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Available from the gdstore.com site, with filler taken from the 7/22/72 show; Soundboard through MR, possibly CX3, to DAT, CD, EAC and SHN; pitch-corrected and normalized by J. Cotsman [2][7]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Paramount Northwest Theatre - Poster](https://www.dead.net/archives/1972/artwork/paramount-northwest-theatre-poster) [13]
